question: Cross-sectional classification of MCI vs cognitively normal (HC/CN) ADNI participants from T1 structural MRI. The task, population class and channel are the same. The features differ within the channel: 8 amygdala shape/volume measures in P-125, and hippocampus+amygdala radiomics fused with 3D-CNN features in P-66.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (P-125 80.00% in its results, 82.14% in its abstract, vs P-66 72.7%); AUC with AUC also available (P-125 85.71-90.31% vs P-66 80).

figures.P-125: 74 subjects (37 MCI/37 HC), 60/40 subject split (about 44 train/30 test), models tuned by 5-fold CV. Mean test accuracy 80.00% (RF and ANN). The reported +/-2.43% is a 95% margin of error across the five fold-models evaluated on the same test partition, not test-sample uncertainty. Wilson on the test set (24/30, n=30): 0.627-0.905. The abstract's 82.14% (23/28) does not appear in the results tables. Test AUC 85.71 (RF) to 90.31 (SVM); Hanley-McNeil for 0.857 (n1=14, n0=16): 0.716-0.999.
figures.P-66: 200 MCI (948 images)/200 CN (853 images); 80/20 image-level split, five repetitions, mean +/- SD. Radiomic+CNN fusion on hippocampus+amygdala: accuracy 72.7 +/- 3.3%, AUC 80.0 +/- 4.6. No interval reported. Wilson on 20% of 1801 images (n=360): 0.679-0.770. The result is robust to n: 0.669-0.778 at n=254 (estimated distinct test subjects) and 0.681-0.768 at n=400. Fold-based check: 72.7 +/- 2.776*3.3/sqrt(5) = 68.6-76.8. Amygdala-only fusion: 70.0 +/- 1.6% (Wilson n=360: 0.651-0.745); amygdala-only radiomics 68.0%; amygdala-only CNN 68.4%. AUC 0.80, Hanley-McNeil with about 190/170 test images: 0.755-0.845.

matched_figure_check: P-66 reports a result under P-125's input condition: the amygdala alone (Table 6), where fusion gives 70.0%, radiomics 68.0% and CNN 68.4%. The matched figure lies further from P-125's 80.00% than P-66's headline does, and 80.00% is outside its interval (0.651-0.745). The matched figure therefore widens the gap rather than dissolving it. P-125 reports nothing under P-66's hippocampal or radiomic condition.
performance_validity: Neither study is flagged: P-125's best test AUC is 90.31% and its accuracy 80.00%; P-66's AUC is 80 and its accuracy 72.7%. Both use internal validation only. P-66's image-level split can place images of one subject in both training and test sets, which would tend to raise P-66's figure, not lower it.

candidate_explanations.difference: Features within the MRI channel: 8 amygdala morphometric scalars (volume, normalised volume, discrete compactness, tortuosity) vs 1746 radiomic features per ROI fused with CNN features.
candidate_explanations.quote: used for training were V, VN, DC, and TR for both hemispheres of the amygdala, for a total of 8 features.

candidate_explanations.difference: Participant selection: P-125 applies strict ADNI criteria (HC MMSE 28-30 and CDR 0; MCI CDR 0.5 with memory impairment), age- and gender-matched, which may yield more separable groups than P-66's random selection of 200 per group.
candidate_explanations.quote: Healthy controls had MMSE scores between 28 and 30, CDR score of 0, and no signs of cognitive impairment or depression.

candidate_explanations.difference: Test-set size: about 30 subjects in P-125 vs about 360 images from 400 subjects in P-66.
candidate_explanations.quote: The machine learning algorithms were trained with the proposed metrics with a partition of 60–40 subjects for training and testing.

candidate_explanations.difference: Split unit: subject-level hold-out (P-125) vs image-level split with several images per subject (P-66). The leakage this allows would favour P-66, so it runs against the observed gap.
candidate_explanations.quote: randomly dividing the MRI data for each classification dataset into a sizeable training and validation set (80 % of images) and a testing set (20 % of images).

candidate_explanations.difference: Classifier and ROI set: RF/SVM/KNN/ANN on the amygdala only vs a radiomics+3D-CNN fusion over hippocampus and amygdala.
candidate_explanations.quote: In the term of MCI vs CN, radiomic- based algorithm alone obtained ACC of 71.6 % and AUC of 77.8, CNN-based algorithm obtained ACC of 69 % and AUC of 75 and their fusion showed ACC of 72.7 % and AUC of 80.

reason: Same question (MCI vs CN in ADNI from T1 MRI) and same metric. P-125's 80.00% lies outside P-66's derived interval for 72.7% (0.679-0.770, robust across plausible n), and P-66's own amygdala-only result (70.0%), which matches P-125's region, is lower still, so the matched figure does not dissolve the gap. Condition 4 holds in one direction only: 72.7% lies inside P-125's Wilson interval on 30 test subjects (0.627-0.905), and a two-sample test is not significant (z = 0.95; z = 1.30 against the amygdala-only 70.0%). P-125's printed +/-2.43% margin would exclude 72.7%, but it measures variation across five fold-models on one test partition, not test-sample uncertainty. Feature set, participant selection, test size, split unit and classifier are candidate explanations, none shown to be sufficient. This is one of the five pairs the operator named; it was judged by the same rule as the others. The record's 82.14% is the abstract figure; the result tables give 80.00%.
